newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss report new discovery against AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss report new discovery against AIDS.

text.p: Scientists at Geneva University have discovered a new protein which blocks the penetration of the AIDS-causing HIV virus into cells in test tubes, Swiss newspaper Journal de Geneve reported on Wednesday.

The French-language daily quoted Robin Offord, a scientist at the university's biochemical medicine division who developed the substance, as saying that the protein, AOP-Rantes, could be developed into a new drug if further tests proved successful.

Unlike traditional drugs taken every day to fight the infection, this protein prevented the virus from entering the cell in the first place but a lengthy series of tests were needed before it could be developed into a drug, Offord said.
"This is a big step in the fight against AIDS and it is not excluded that it can be used as a medicine in the future," he said.
The World Health Organisation, the U.N. health agency, estimates that AIDS may affect nearly 30 million adults by 2000 and is killing one million people every year.
